P.text: Rewards and slashing amounts are read on demand from an external source (ValidatorManager) when computing the exchange ratio in StakingAccountant::_getExchangeRatio; rewards may be accredited in intervals longer than StakingManager::withdrawalDelay.
P.evidence_quote: Because the rewards and slashing amounts are read on demand from an external source, an attacker can front-run rewards and slashing events and potentially game the system.

I.text: The exchange ratio calculation should not be manipulable by front-running reward and slashing events, so that staking and withdrawal timing cannot be used to capture rewards or avoid penalties.
I.evidence_quote: Users are incentivized to stake immediately before rewards events occur, which undermines the protocol’s intended distribution of rewards. Similarly, users could `queueWithdrawal` their funds just prior to a slashing event to avoid incurring the associated penalties, compromising the protocol’s fairness and stability.

V.text: An attacker can front-run reward events by staking to receive rewards and front-run slashing events by queueWithdrawal to avoid penalties; for sufficiently large amounts this can yield significant profits.
V.evidence_quote: For sufficiently large amounts, exploiting this vulnerability can yield significant profits.
